sources.notes: Banner reads Issue 9 - January 15, 2025; subtitle Standard for Technical Documentation; legal notice: copyright and trademark of ASD, EU Trade Mark No. 017966390; footer Copyright 2026 STEMG. Page shows no publication date.

sources.title: About ASD-STE100
sources.notes: 53 writing rules in 9 sections; approximately 900 approved words and approximately 1,200 not-approved words; Issue 9 released 2025-01-15; 555 dictionary entries updated; terminology aligned with ISO 1087-1:2019 with the designations technical nouns and technical verbs; 17 releases in total.

sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions, ASD-STE100
sources.notes: Free of charge, PDF is the only distribution format; Issue 10 scheduled for January 2028; issues usually every three years; ASD and STEMG do not endorse or certify tool vendors; -ing forms only as technical nouns; passive only in descriptive text when the agent is unknown; American English and Merriam-Webster; EU trade mark granted 2006 and 2018.

sources.title: Tools for STE
sources.notes: Disclaimer: ASD and STEMG do not endorse, certify, or authorize any software tools, including AI-based ones; vendors may not claim ASD approval or use the logo, copyright or trademark. Guidance on what checkers can and cannot verify.

sources.title: ASD-STE100 Issue 9: Setting a standard for technical documentation
sources.notes: February 2025 issue (exact day not shown). States that the earlier terms technical name and technical verb were replaced by technical noun and technical verb (term); no new rules, 31 of 53 reworded; 555 dictionary entries updated; specification up to Issue 8, 2021; Issue 9 released 2025-01-15.

sources.title: Term checker rules for ASD-STE100 issue 9
sources.notes: Public index of Issue 9 rule numbers with short paraphrased titles and whether a term checker can verify each. Published date is the page-updated date shown on the page. Used only for rule numbering and topics.

sources.title: Term checker rules for ASD-STE100 issue 8 (archived page)
sources.notes: Uses the Issue 8 term technical names (TNs), which confirms the pre-Issue 9 wording.

sources.title: Simplified Technical English
sources.notes: Last edited 2026-10-05. Secondary overview; reports free distribution since Issue 6 (2013), distribution counts, and a paraphrased rule list. Numbers treated as reported.

sources.title: OneRead: a compiler for technical English (ASD-STE100 Issue 9 mechanical checker)
sources.notes: MIT. Python stdlib, regex only, no dictionary, no passive check. 0 stars, created and last pushed 2026-08-13 (GitHub API, 2026-10-10). Studied, not copied.

sources.title: ste-lint: Simplified Technical English prose linter
sources.notes: MIT. Rust. 4 stars. Offset-preserving markdown masks, abbreviation-aware sentence splitter, regex passive and -ing heuristics.

sources.title: Ste100Mark: .NET Markdown linter for ASD-STE100-style rules
sources.notes: MIT. C#. 0 stars, last pushed 2026-10-05. Word-count normalization, stative participle exclusions, rule catalog with official/mechanical/advisory classification, bring-your-own dictionary.

sources.title: asd-ste100-checker: spaCy-based STE checker with CLI, MCP and LSP
sources.notes: Apache-2.0. Python. 21 stars. Dependency-based passive detection, imperative detection, noun runs of 4 or more. The repository commits the official Issue 9 PDF and extracted dictionary data; that material was not used.

sources.title: agent-simple-english: TypeScript STE rule engine with wink-nlp tagging
sources.notes: MIT. TypeScript, package version 0.7.0, 11 stars, last pushed 2026-10-09. Hard and soft severities; token-level passive, progressive and perfect detection; data files with provenance fields.

sources.title: asd-ste100-skill: STE for software documentation, with a 19-rule stdlib linter
sources.notes: GitHub license field NOASSERTION; LICENSE file is the MIT text. Python. 8 stars. Placeholder protection for code, links, URLs, emails; imperative starter list; terminology drift.

sources.title: ASD-STE100 Claude Code plugin, skill and JavaScript linter
sources.notes: MIT. JavaScript. 5 stars. Heuristic engine without POS tagging; exclusion sets for -ing nouns and -ed nouns; stop-list noun cluster detection.

sources.title: Simplified Technical English skill with ste_check.py
sources.notes: GitHub license field NOASSERTION; LICENSE file MIT with a NOTICE on ASD copyright. Python. 965 stars. Ships a word list derived from the Issue 7 (2017) dictionary, which was not used.

sources.title: ASD-STE100 skill for agent output, with ste-lint.py
sources.notes: MIT. Python. 4,325 stars, last pushed 2026-10-04. Regex passive with irregular participle list; advisory findings never fail; explicitly no noun-cluster rule.

sources.title: SimpleEnglish agent skill with mechanical STE linter and local dictionary extractor
sources.notes: MIT. Python. 3,857 stars, last pushed 2026-10-05. Linter mirrors OneRead (no passive check); the dictionary tool builds word lists from the user's own PDF and gitignores them.

sources.title: vale-llm-slop: Vale styles inspired by ASD-STE100
sources.notes: GitHub license field NOASSERTION; LICENSE file MIT. 27 stars, last pushed 2026-09-15. POS-sequence rules: PassiveVoice (be + VBN), Gerunds (VBG), NounClusters (four NN/NNS/NNP), SentenceLength 25, ProcedureLength.

sources.title: doc-standards: documentation quality skill with a lint gate
sources.notes: MIT. Python. 18 stars. check_docs.py: sentence length, regex passive skipped on step items, present perfect, terminology drift, heading hierarchy.

sources.title: compromise: modest natural-language processing (repository)
Compromise API Reference (docs/api.md)
sources.notes: Read from the cloned repository at commit 2e7a1b9. Lists .sentences(), .verbs(), .nouns(), .clauses(), .chunks(), .match(), .has(), .if(), .ifNo(), .before(), .after(), .splitOn(), .splitBefore(), .splitAfter(), .fullSentences(), .wordCount(), .compute(), nlp.tokenize(text, lexicon?), nlp.plugin(), nlp.addWords(words, isFrozen?).

sources.title: Compromise Tags, part-of-speech tagset (docs/tag-definitions.md)
sources.notes: Defines #Gerund, #Imperative, #Infinitive, #Participle, #Passive, #PastTense, #PresentTense, #Modal, #Auxiliary, #Copula, #PhrasalVerb, #Particle, #Noun, #Singular, #Plural, #ProperNoun, #Acronym, #Url, #Email, #Abbreviation, #Condition and others.

sources.title: compromise verb grammar forms (forms.js)
sources.notes: Source of the grammar.form values: imperative, infinitive, simple-present, simple-past, simple-future, present/past/future-progressive, present/past/future-perfect, perfect-progressive variants, passive-present, passive-past, passive-future, present-conditional, past-conditional, gerund-phrase, want-infinitive.

sources.title: compromise imperative tagging pass (08-imperative.js)
sources.notes: Heuristic that assigns #Imperative to a sentence-initial infinitive or Noun|Verb switch word followed by a noun or determiner.

sources.title: compromise URL and email token recognition (web.js)
sources.notes: Regexes for emails, explicit URLs and bare domains so they survive tokenization as one term.

sources.title: compromise phrasal verb lexicon (phrasals.js)
sources.notes: 945 two-word phrasal verbs, MIT, credited to allmyphrasalverbs.com. Candidate source for the linter's phrasal-verb list.
